StreinuTheran2009 supplies the sparse-hypergraph pebble decision, extraction, and component machinery.
LeiRoss2023 gives O3 sufficiency, not this exact O3-versus-relation-rank separation witness.
SrivastavaPimentel2022 gives the reciprocal-relation-singular-value projection perturbation antecedent, but not the shell-uniform causal-mean risk bound.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 2 — pebble algorithm
novelty_flags.one_line: The stated pebble-game decision, extraction, and tight-component output is an application of Streinu and Theran's published sparse-hypergraph algorithms, not an independent theorem-level novelty claim.

novelty_flags.label: Comparator promise and Theorem 1/Proposition 1
novelty_flags.one_line: The prose presents a strict improvement over LeiRoss2023's O3 screen, but no statement explicitly asserts O3 acceptance implies the pebble certificate and that the four-mask construction makes this inclusion strict.

soundness_flags.label: def:anchor-hypergraph and thm:pebble-full-law
soundness_flags.one_line: The anchor pairs are chosen without a deterministic rule or an anchor-invariance assertion, while the theorem's rank condition depends on the resulting H3; moreover, 'every admissible loading mean' is not defined.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:shell-deformation; thm:minimax-frontier; thm:honest-rectangle
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The lower experiment is conditional on an affirmative uniform legal-shell deformation result; nonempty shells alone may lack the primitive slack needed by that construction.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The minimax-risk and honest-width frontiers are claimed conditional on a positive resolution of Open-ended Question 1, unless the shell is revised to impose an explicit quantitative interior-slack condition.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3–4, Introduction; p. 16, Theorem 3; p. 22, Theorem 4 and equations (9)–(11)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper identifies counterfactual means under O3 convergence and proves fixed-T consistency/asymptotic linearity; its sparse-panel theorem has inverse dependence on the positive APM eigenvalue.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1, abstract; pp. 8–9, Section 3.2 and equation (3.2); p. 20, Section 6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper constructs four-block subproblems from staggered-adoption panels and proves entrywise inference with an instance-wise lower-bound comparison.
The paper gives weak-factor testing and confidence-interval width lower bounds in its large-factor entrywise-learning model.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1, Theorem 1; p. 4, proof discussion following Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 bounds canonical-projection subspace error through a noise-to-signal ratio and a reciprocal smallest-singular-value term.

The published pebble-game framework recognizes sparse/tight/dependent hypergraphs, extracts independent structures, and supplies component machinery; specializing it to the supplied 3-uniform anchor hypergraph yields the algorithmic portion of Theorem 2.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a deterministic anchor-pair convention or prove that every allowable anchor choice has the same rank, and define the quantified class of admissible loading means in the full-law theorem.

Replace the standalone pebble-algorithm theorem with a panel-specific reduction theorem, explicitly proving O3 acceptance implies the pebble certificate and that the four-mask witness makes the inclusion strict against LeiRoss2023.

Resolve the deformation question on a quantitatively interior shell, or formulate and prove a necessary slack condition that exactly separates deformable from boundary-tight shells before asserting universal minimax and honest-width frontiers.

recommended_next_step: Revise the anchor and comparator statements, demote the imported pebble algorithm to background, and carry the field-tier statistical frontier forward only in its explicit shell-deformation-conditional form.
